山田水車屋.name: Yamada Suisha-ya
山田水車屋.desc: An ultra-unique Okinawa soba shop that used to be in Yamada, Onna Village (* closed in December 2021). Famous for its handmade bungee jump and the goats it kept, its bonito-broth Suisha Soba was a reasonable ¥500. I'm keeping this article as a record.
t: I ate here in April 2021 😄
Note: Unfortunately this shop is now closed. I'm writing it down as a record.

Near the entrance of the now-gone “Yamada Suisha-ya.” The exterior was impactful too, so I wish I had taken a photo showing the whole exterior ^^; It closed, maybe due to the effects of COVID, which is a pity.
There was a bungee jump too. They also kept goats. Unique, lol
The stairs leading to the bungee jump 😁 Full of a handmade feel, lol
Suisha soba　¥500
I ordered the “Suisha Soba” recommended by the owner. A bonito-broth-forward soup with thin wavy noodles. It was just plain tasty, and the price was reasonable too.

Rating (9/15): It was just plain tasty, but it's a pity it has closed. What stuck with me is that when I ate there, the owner was happily chatting with other tourists. I also vaguely remember there was something handmade inside like a “COVID sterilization device?”, but it was a very unique shop 😁

島そば.name: Shima Soba
島そば.desc: A long-established shop along Prefectural Route 255 in Enohi, Uruma City. A popular local shop with a hand-lettered-looking sign full of character, whose charm is the double-stock broth that is bonito-based but with a strong pork-bone presence, and melt-in-your-mouth braised pork belly. Shima soba, large, is a reasonable ¥650. Next door is Tsuki Kuroki.
t: I went to eat here in February 2023 😊
Shima Soba (the sign seems hand-lettered? and has great character, lol)
Menu
I ordered the “shima soba,” which shares the shop's name
Shima soba, large　¥650

The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is melt-in-your-mouth and delicious. The noodles are medium-thick, and the broth is bonito-based but I also feel a strong pork-bone flavor 😊 They seem to have raised prices recently due to rising raw material costs, but even so I think ¥650 for large is cheap 😁
Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty. Why not stop by when you come near Enohi in Uruma City? There seems to be another Okinawa soba shop right next door, so I'd like to take that on next time.

島そば一番地.name: Shima Soba Ichibanchi
島そば一番地.desc: The Naha branch of a Yaeyama soba specialty shop whose main store is on Ishigaki Island. Shima soba with thinly sliced fish cake and braised pork belly, round thin noodles, and a faintly pork-bone broth, served with a mini miso rice ball. Changing the flavor with pipaz spice is the Yaeyama way too.
t: I ate here in February 2024 😄
It's on the 2nd floor of Nōren Plaza
Shima Soba Ichibanchi
Shima Soba Ichibanchi
This soba shop is a Yaeyama soba specialty shop, and it seems to run two shops: the main store on Ishigaki Island, and this Naha branch (Hikawa, Naha City) on the Okinawa main island.

A comment from an island-song singer written on the menu. I wonder if he's famous (^0^;)
From the menu I decided to order the “shima soba,” which shares the shop's name.
Explanation of the effects of pipaz spice
Perhaps as a feature of Yaeyama soba, there's a spice called “pipaz,” and it seems to have various effects 😄 I'd like to try it partway through to change the flavor 😆
Shima soba, medium　¥700 (in the back there is also pipaz spice)
The shima soba has arrived 😄 Not only pickles but also a mini rice ball (miso) comes with it, which is a good deal 😆
I previously had Yaeyama soba for the first time at “Miyara Soba (Urasoe branch)” in Urasoe City, and the feature is that the fish cake and braised pork belly are thinly sliced.
First, a sip of the broth. A broth with a faint pork-bone base, just plain tasty.
Shima soba, medium　¥700
Next, the noodles. They are thin straight noodles, on the soft side. The braised pork belly and fish cake are just plain tasty too.
Partway through I added “pipaz” to change the flavor 😆 But it tasted like ordinary pepper? and wasn't the spice I'd imagined (^0^;)

Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty. If you want to try Yaeyama soba, why not give this shop a try once? I used a paid coin parking lot nearby without knowing, but apparently the Nōren Plaza parking lot is free for one hour 😄

島人そば.name: Shimanchu Soba
島人そば.desc: A sister shop of the tacos-famous “Gate One.” Its signature is the Shimanchu Soba, with a broth of Agu pork stock scented with bonito, and it was also selected as one of the “Tabearuki Kyushu-Okinawa 100 Taste Shops.” Its longer hours, until 20:30, are convenient too.
t: * This article was created with “Chat gpt4o” and partly supplemented by me, lol
I went to eat here in August 2024 😆
Shimanchu Soba
Shimanchu Soba
The menu says it is a sister shop of Gate One, a taco and taco rice shop.
Even the tissue packs advertise Gate One 😆

Incidentally, I'm told this is a sister shop of the shop called “Gate One,” famous for taco rice and tacos. As usual I went in with no research, so I learned this for the first time (^0^;) The tacos looked famous and delicious too, but this time, since I aim to conquer every Okinawa soba shop, I ordered the “Shimanchu Soba” 😆
Furthermore, the menu says it was selected as one of the “Tabearuki Kyushu-Okinawa 100 Taste Shops.” I don't really know what that is, but maybe I can expect something 😄
Menu (my smartphone was overheating and the photo is out of focus. Sorry 🙏)
Menu
Menu
Inside the shop
Inside the shop (I don't know who, but there are many autographs of celebrities too)

When you enter the shop, a calm, Okinawan atmosphere spreads out first. Autograph boards of celebrities are lined up along the wall, giving the impression of a shop loved by locals and tourists alike. It's also nice that you can get water and tea self-service, so casual. Wrapped in a relaxed atmosphere, I looked at the menu right away, and what caught my eye was, as expected, the “Shimanchu Soba.” A soba with the same name as the shop — I have to order it!
Shimanchu soba　¥800

After ordering and waiting a while, the “Shimanchu Soba” finally arrived. In a big bowl, the generous broth and medium-thick noodles whet the appetite. The broth, said to use “Agu stock,” gives a distinct pork flavor on the first sip, but at the same time the aroma of bonito comes through too.
Shimanchu soba　¥800

The noodles are medium-thin, with a characteristically soft texture. I felt they were slightly lacking in firmness and thought a bit more bite would be good~ But they cling easily to the broth and were perfect for the light, easy-to-drink broth.

The toppings include braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). The braised pork belly is lightly seasoned. The soft-bone pork ribs are also lightly seasoned, a bit firm, with some sinewy texture remaining. This may divide opinions, but for those who want to enjoy a solid texture, it might be a plus. I prefer them a bit softer, but those who like this meat's chew might like it.

Rating (9/15): Overall, the “Shimanchu Soba” didn't have strong surprise or individuality, and my impression was of a so-called “just plain tasty” soba. The shop's hours are 11:00 to 20:30, which I think is longer than the hours of other Okinawa soba shops. If you get a chance to come to Yogi in Okinawa City, please do stop by “Shimanchu Soba.” Next time I'd like to try the tacos too 😆

縁そば.name: En Soba
縁そば.desc: Moved from Gakuen-dori in Iso to inside Makeman Urasoe. The signature En Soba has a broth with the umami of pork bone, kelp, and bonito flakes and chewy whole-wheat noodles. A noodle shop with mazesoba, ramen, and even a fried chicken set.
t: ― 2nd Visit (March 2025) ―
I went to “Mendokoro En Soba” inside Makeman in Gusukuma, Urasoe City 😊 I went to eat in March 2025 😄
En Soba is inside Makeman
En Soba

What I had this time was the “En Soba, large,” which has the same name as the shop. I had eaten here before, when it was on Gakuen-dori in Iso, Urasoe City, so this is my first visit since then. This was my first time since it moved here, so I headed over looking forward to how it would be 🚗✨ Since it's inside Makeman, there's almost no worry about parking, which is really helpful. It's easy to stop by while shopping, and the location seems easy for families and locals to use.

In front of the shop is a big yellow “En Soba” noren, which was quite eye-catching 🌼 As it's a restaurant inside a home improvement store, at first I imagined something closer to a food court, but it was actually a proper standalone shop, with a calm interior. The wood-grain floor and tables give warmth, and the seating seemed relatively roomy. It looks easy to use at lunchtime or after shopping, and I like the atmosphere of casually eating Okinawa soba 🍜
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu

Looking at the menu, there was quite a variety just in Okinawa soba. En soba, tebichi soba, braised pork belly soba, soft-bone pork ribs soba, meat and bean sprouts soba, small soba, and more were lined up, and there are also seafood mazesoba, Taiwan mazesoba, ramen dishes, and even a fried chicken set 😳 Rather than an Okinawa soba shop, it's more of a noodle place where you can eat a wide range. The fried chicken set also looks good value, and seems good for those who want to eat heartily. This time I ordered the signature-looking “En Soba, large” without hesitation.
En soba, large　¥950

The bowl that arrived after a while looks like a classic Okinawa soba just from appearance ✨ On a brownish broth sit medium-thin noodles, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), fish cake (kamaboko), shredded egg, and green onions, a look that is not too flashy but well put together. The bowl is also subdued, matching the broth's color, and looked delicious.

Starting with the broth, it seems to be made from pork bone, kelp, and bonito flakes, with firm umami. I can feel the mellowness of the pork bone, but overall the bonito flavor comes slightly to the front 🐟 I thought it's still a delicious broth as ever 😋
En soba, large　¥950

The noodles are medium-thin, slightly wavy noodles kneaded with whole-wheat flour. When lifted with chopsticks they look smooth, and when eaten they're chewy 🍜✨ They're slurpy, easy-to-eat noodles. Since they contain whole wheat, they have a slightly different presence from ordinary noodles 😊

Since the toppings include braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs, it looks satisfying as well. The braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs are tender too 🥩 My honest impression is that both are tender but the sinewy texture bothered me a little. Because the impressions of the broth and noodles are so good, if the meat toppings had been finished a bit more meltingly, the overall satisfaction would have risen further. The flavor isn't bad, so it was truly just a little short, I felt 🤔

The fish cake, shredded egg, and green onions are included too, giving the proper reassurance of Okinawa soba. Especially the shredded egg gives a touch of brightness to the look 🌿 The aroma of the green onions suits the broth, balancing the whole. Rather than a flashy impact, it's a bowl that lets you take a breather in the middle of shopping. Including its location inside Makeman, I think it's an Okinawa soba shop easy to use in daily life. Even with a family, there are many menu choices, so those who want Okinawa soba, those who want mazesoba, and those who want to add fried chicken could each be satisfied 👍

Rating (10/15): This time's “En Soba, large” was an easy-to-eat bowl with a well-balanced broth and slurpy, chewy noodles 🍜 While both pork bone and bonito umami can be felt, the broth with a slight bonito lean has stability. The noodles with whole wheat have character and went well with the broth. However, it was a pity that the braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs toppings had a little sinewy texture. If that were improved, it would become a highly satisfying bowl. Even so, I'm glad I can eat Okinawa soba of this level while shopping at Makeman 😊 It's easy to enter, the menu is extensive, and it was a shop where I want to try other menu items again.
― 1st Visit (October 2023) ―
I ate here in October 2023. This shop is a participating shop in the “13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29),” and I went as the 4th of 34 shops 😊
En Soba is along Gakuen-dori near Pipeline-dori.
It seems this shop's lease expires at the end of December 2023, but the relocation site hasn't been decided. Because of that, and the stamp rally running until December, I decided to go early 😁
The stamp rally booklet featured the “En Soba,” which has the same name as the shop, so I had planned to order the “En Soba,” and the menu also introduces it as the owner's recommendation.
Menu

This shop has not only Okinawa soba but also mazesoba and ramen. Previously I thought the Okinawa soba at the ramen shop “Ajisen Ramen” on the Okinawa Expressway (Nakagusuku SA) was of quite a high level, so I can expect this shop's Okinawa soba too 🤗
En soba, medium　¥800

First the broth. The moment I drank it: “Delicious” 😊 The menu says “Our proud broth, carefully simmered with selected pork bone, kelp, and bonito flakes,” and it's a gentle, delicious broth with a bonito stock lean.

Next, the noodles. The explanation said “Please enjoy the chewy, slurpy texture of the noodles kneaded with whole-wheat flour,” and indeed, they were chewy thin straight noodles, and these were delicious too 🤤
En soba, medium　¥800　Slurpy, chewy noodles, delicious.

Rating (10/15): There might be a rule that “Okinawa soba shops that also serve ramen are high level” 🤗 The bonito-based broth and chewy whole-wheat noodles were high level and delicious. However, the braised pork belly was a little sinewy, which was a pity~. The relocation site after the end of December 2023 hasn't been decided, but I think it's delicious Okinawa soba, so I hope they somehow find a new location and keep operating.
